```{python}
import os
import math
import requests
import pandas as pd
from typing import List, Dict, Optional


BASE_URL = "https://data.mo.gov"
DATASET_ID = "hcm8-fbau"  # CNA-Approved-Facility-Training-Agencies

def fetch_socrata_dataset(
    dataset_id: str,
    base_url: str = BASE_URL,
    app_token: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: int = 50000,        # SODA allows large page sizes; adjust if needed
    where: Optional[str] = None,
    select: Optional[str] = None,
    order: Optional[str] = None
) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Fetch all rows from a Socrata dataset using pagination.
    Returns a list of JSON records (dicts).
    """
    session = requests.Session()
    headers = {}
    if app_token:
        headers["X-App-Token"] = app_token

    resource_url = f"{base_url}/resource/{dataset_id}.json"
    rows: List[Dict] = []
    offset = 0

    while True:
        params = {"$limit": limit, "$offset": offset}
        if where:  params["$where"]  = where
        if select: params["$select"] = select
        if order:  params["$order"]  = order

        resp = session.get(resource_url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=30)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        batch = resp.json()

        if not batch:
            break

        rows.extend(batch)
        # Stop when the returned batch is smaller than the page size
        if len(batch) < limit:
            break

        offset += limit

    return rows

def to_dataframe(rows: List[Dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    # Optional: normalize common date/number fields if present
    # Example:
    # if "approval_date" in df:
    #     df["approval_date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["approval_date"], errors="coerce")
    return df

def main():
    # Optional: set an app token to raise rate limits (create one in your Socrata account)
    app_token = os.getenv("SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN", None)

    # Example filters (uncomment and adjust once you know field names)
    # where = "city = 'Jefferson City'"
    # select = "agency_name, city, county, approval_date"
    # order  = "agency_name"

    rows = fetch_socrata_dataset(
        DATASET_ID,
        app_token=app_token,
        # where=where,
        # select=select,
        # order=order,
    )

    df = to_dataframe(rows)

    # Preview
    print(f"Total rows: {len(df)}")
    print(df.head(10))

    # Save outputs
    csv_path = "C:/Users/urbonn/Documents/Analysis frequent customes/temp/cna_approved_training_agencies.csv"
    xlsx_path = "C:/Users/urbonn/Documents/Analysis frequent customes/temp/cna_approved_training_agencies.xlsx"
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False, encoding="utf-8")
    # Excel writer requires openpyxl installed
  #  with pd.ExcelWriter(xlsx_path, engine="openpyxl") as writer:
   #     df.to_excel(writer, index=False, sheet_name="agencies")

with pd.ExcelWriter("output.xlsx", engine="openpyxl", mode="w") as writer:
    df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Sheet1", index=False)
    wb = writer.book
    for ws in wb.worksheets:
        ws.sheet_state = "visible"
    wb.active = 0

    print(f"Saved: {csv_path}")
    print(f"Saved: {xlsx_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```{python}


import re
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd
from tqdm import tqdm

# ----------------------------
# Configuration
# ----------------------------
BASE_URL = "https://montanaworks.gov"
START_URL = "https://montanaworks.gov/training"
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("C:/Users/urbonn/Documents/Analysis frequent customes/temp/")
SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.headers.update({
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
                  "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
                  "Chrome/123.0 Safari/537.36 Nan-WIOA-ETPL-Fetcher"
})
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 20
DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0
DOWNLOAD_EXTS = {".csv", ".xlsx", ".xls", ".json", ".pdf"}

# Terms used to identify relevant links
TEXT_TERMS = [
    "wioa",
    "eligible training provider",
    "eligible training providers",
    "etpl",
]
URL_TERMS = [
    "wioa", "etpl", "eligible-training", "eligible_training",
]

# ----------------------------
# Helpers
# ----------------------------
def ensure_output() -> None:
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def clean_filename(name: str) -> str:
    name = re.sub(r"[^\w\-.]+", "_", name).strip("_")
    return name[:150] or "file"

def get_html(url: str) -> BeautifulSoup:
    """
    Basic HTML fetch using requests, with a polite delay and error handling.
    """
    time.sleep(DELAY_SECONDS)
    resp = SESSION.get(url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "lxml")

def score_link(a_tag, page_url: str) -> Tuple[int, str]:
    """
    Score a link by relevance to WIOA ETPL.
    Returns (score, absolute_url).
    """
    href = a_tag.get("href")
    text = a_tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    if not href:
        return (0, "")

    abs_url = urljoin(page_url, href)
    score = 0
    txt = (text or "").lower()
    url_lower = abs_url.lower()

    # Text signals
    for term in TEXT_TERMS:
        if term in txt:
            score += 5

    # URL signals
    for term in URL_TERMS:
        if term in url_lower:
            score += 3

    # Prefer direct data files
    ext = Path(urlparse(abs_url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        score += 2

    # Prefer staying within /training
    if urlparse(abs_url).path.startswith("/training"):
        score += 1

    return (score, abs_url)

def find_candidate_links(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str, str]]:
    """
    Return a list of (score, url, link_text), sorted by score(desc).
    """
    candidates = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        score, abs_url = score_link(a, page_url)
        if score > 0:
            candidates.append((score, abs_url, a.get_text(" ", strip=True)))
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    return candidates

def download_file(url: str, filename_hint: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Path]:
    """
    Download a file to OUTPUT_DIR and return the saved path.
    """
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    ext = Path(parsed.path).suffix.lower()
    fname = filename_hint or Path(parsed.path).name or "download"
    if ext and not fname.lower().endswith(ext):
        fname += ext
    fname = clean_filename(fname)
    out_path = OUTPUT_DIR / fname

    with SESSION.get(url, stream=True, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        total = int(r.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        chunk = 1024 * 64
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f, tqdm(
            total=total if total > 0 else None,
            unit="B", unit_scale=True, unit_divisor=1024,
            desc=f"Downloading {fname}",
            leave=False
        ) as pbar:
            for c in r.iter_content(chunk_size=chunk):
                if c:
                    f.write(c)
                    if total > 0:
                        pbar.update(len(c))
    print(f"✔ Saved file: {out_path}")
    return out_path

def save_tables_from_page(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> int:
    """
    Extract any HTML tables on the page and save as CSV.
    """
    html = str(soup)
    try:
        tables = pd.read_html(html)
    except ValueError:
        tables = []

    if not tables:
        return 0

    slug = clean_filename(Path(urlparse(page_url).path).name or "training")
    count = 0
    for i, df in enumerate(tables, start=1):
        out_path = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{slug}_table_{i}.csv"
        df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
        count += 1
    print(f"✔ Extracted {count} table(s) from {page_url}")
    return count

def process_candidate(url: str, link_text: str) -> None:
    """
    If candidate is a direct file -> download
    Else -> open the page, try to extract tables and find file links.
    """
    ext = Path(urlparse(url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        download_file(url, filename_hint=link_text or Path(urlparse(url).path).name)
        return

    # Not a direct file: open the page
    try:
        soup = get_html(url)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"❌ Failed to open {url}: {e}")
        return

    # Try tables first
    saved_tables = save_tables_from_page(soup, url)

    # Also search on this page for more direct file links
    file_links = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = urljoin(url, a["href"])
        ext2 = Path(urlparse(href).path).suffix.lower()
        if ext2 in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
            text2 = a.get_text(" ", strip=True) or Path(urlparse(href).path).name
            score = 0
            t2 = (text2 or "").lower()
            for term in TEXT_TERMS:
                if term in t2:
                    score += 3
            file_links.append((score, href, text2))

    file_links.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)

    for _, href, text2 in file_links:
        try:
            download_file(href, filename_hint=text2)
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            print(f"❌ Failed to download {href}: {e}")

    if saved_tables == 0 and not file_links:
        print(f"ℹ No tables or data files found on {url}. "
              f"If the page is JavaScript-rendered, use the Selenium variant.")

def find_wioa_etpl() -> None:
    ensure_output()

    # Load the training start page
    try:
        soup = get_html(START_URL)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"❌ Failed to open {START_URL}: {e}")
        return

    # Find candidate links on the training page
    candidates = find_candidate_links(soup, START_URL)

    if not candidates:
        print("⚠ No links mentioning WIOA/ETPL found on the training page.")
    else:
        print("🔎 Candidate links (top 10):")
        for i, (score, url, text) in enumerate(candidates[:10], start=1):
            print(f"  {i}. score={score} | text='{text}' | url={url}")

    # Process the best candidate
    if candidates:
        best_score, best_url, best_text = candidates[0]
        print(f"\n➡ Processing best match: score={best_score}, text='{best_text}', url={best_url}\n")
        process_candidate(best_url, best_text)

    # Manifest
    manifest = {"start_url": START_URL}
    with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
    print(f"📒 Wrote manifest to {OUTPUT_DIR / 'manifest.json'}")
    print("✅ Done.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    find_wioa_etpl()




from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager

def get_html(url: str) -> BeautifulSoup:
    options = webdriver.ChromeOptions()
    options.add_argument("--headless=new")
    driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=Service(ChromeDriverManager().install()), options=options)
    try:
        driver.get(url)
        time.sleep(2.5)  # allow JS to render
        html = driver.page_source
        return BeautifulSoup(html, "lxml")
    finally:
        driver.quit()
```

```{python}
import time
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd


from datetime import datetime
import shutil

# Standard export names (date-stamped)
RUN_DATE = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
EXPORT_CSV = f"WIOA_ETPL_Montana_{RUN_DATE}.csv"
EXPORT_XLSX = f"WIOA_ETPL_Montana_{RUN_DATE}.xlsx"

def export_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> Path:
    """Export the combined dataframe to CSV (and optionally Excel) in OUTPUT_DIR."""
    out_csv = OUTPUT_DIR / EXPORT_CSV
    df.to_csv(out_csv, index=False)
    print(f"📄 Exported combined CSV: {out_csv}")

    # Optional: also write Excel (requires XlsxWriter)
    try:
        with pd.ExcelWriter(OUTPUT_DIR / EXPORT_XLSX, engine="xlsxwriter") as writer:
            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="ETPL", index=False)
        print(f"📊 Exported Excel: {OUTPUT_DIR / EXPORT_XLSX}")
    except Exception as e:
        # Don’t fail the run because Excel export failed
        print(f"ℹ Skipped Excel export (install 'XlsxWriter' to enable). Reason: {e}")

    return out_csv

def read_file_as_dataframe(file_path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Try reading a downloaded file as a dataframe (CSV/XLSX)."""
    ext = file_path.suffix.lower()
    if ext == ".csv":
        return pd.read_csv(file_path)
    if ext in {".xlsx", ".xls"}:
        return pd.read_excel(file_path)
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format for DataFrame conversion: {ext}")


# --------------------------------
# Config
# --------------------------------
START_URL = "https://montanaworks.gov/training"
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("C:/Users/urbonn/Documents/Analysis frequent customes/temp/")
TPUT_DIR = Path("C:/Users/urbonn/Documents/Analysis frequent customes/temp/")
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 20
DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0
DOWNLOAD_EXTS = {".csv", ".xlsx", ".xls", ".json", ".pdf"}

SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.headers.update({
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
                  "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
                  "Chrome/123.0 Safari/537.36 Nan-WIOA-ETPL-Fetcher"
})

TEXT_TERMS = ["wioa", "eligible training provider", "eligible training providers", "etpl"]
URL_TERMS  = ["wioa", "etpl", "eligible-training", "eligible_training"]

# --------------------------------
# Helpers
# --------------------------------
def ensure_output() -> None:
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def clean_filename(name: str) -> str:
    name = re.sub(r"[^\w\-.]+", "_", name).strip("_")
    return name[:150] or "file"

def get_html(url: str) -> BeautifulSoup:
    """Fetch HTML and return BeautifulSoup object."""
    time.sleep(DELAY_SECONDS)
    resp = SESSION.get(url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "lxml")

def score_link(a_tag, page_url: str) -> Tuple[int, str]:
    href = a_tag.get("href")
    text = a_tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    if not href:
        return (0, "")
    abs_url = urljoin(page_url, href)
    score = 0
    txt = (text or "").lower()
    url_lower = abs_url.lower()

    for term in TEXT_TERMS:
        if term in txt:
            score += 5
    for term in URL_TERMS:
        if term in url_lower:
            score += 3

    ext = Path(urlparse(abs_url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        score += 2
    if urlparse(abs_url).path.startswith("/training"):
        score += 1

    return (score, abs_url)

def find_candidate_links(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str, str]]:
    candidates = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        score, abs_url = score_link(a, page_url)
        if score > 0:
            candidates.append((score, abs_url, a.get_text(" ", strip=True)))
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    return candidates

def download_file(url: str, filename_hint: Optional[str] = None) -> Path:
    """Download a file to OUTPUT_DIR; if CSV/XLSX, also export to the standard name."""
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    ext = Path(parsed.path).suffix.lower()
    fname = filename_hint or Path(parsed.path).name or "download"
    if ext and not fname.lower().endswith(ext):
        fname += ext
    saved_path = OUTPUT_DIR / clean_filename(fname)

    r = SESSION.get(url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
    r.raise_for_status()
    with open(saved_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(r.content)
    print(f"✔ Saved file: {saved_path}")

    # If it’s a CSV/XLSX, also produce a standard export file
    try:
        if ext in {".csv", ".xlsx", ".xls"}:
            df = read_file_as_dataframe(saved_path)
            export_dataframe(df)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ℹ Could not create standardized export from {saved_path}: {e}")

    return saved_path

def save_tables_from_page(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> int:
    """Extract HTML tables on the page, save individual CSVs, and export a combined CSV."""
    try:
        tables = pd.read_html(str(soup))
    except ValueError:
        tables = []

    if not tables:
        return 0

    slug = clean_filename(Path(urlparse(page_url).path).name or "training")
    combined = []
    count = 0
    for i, df in enumerate(tables, start=1):
        out_path = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{slug}_table_{i}.csv"
        df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
        combined.append(df)
        count += 1

    print(f"✔ Extracted {count} table(s) from {page_url}")

    # Export a combined file (stack rows; align columns by name)
    try:
        combined_df = pd.concat(combined, ignore_index=True)
        export_dataframe(combined_df)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ℹ Could not combine tables: {e}")

    return count

def process_candidate(url: str, link_text: str) -> None:
    ext = Path(urlparse(url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        download_file(url, filename_hint=link_text or Path(urlparse(url).path).name)
        return

    try:
        soup = get_html(url)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"❌ Failed to open {url}: {e}")
        return

    saved_tables = save_tables_from_page(soup, url)

    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = urljoin(url, a["href"])
        text2 = a.get_text(" ", strip=True) or Path(urlparse(href).path).name
        ext2 = Path(urlparse(href).path).suffix.lower()
        if ext2 in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
            try:
                download_file(href, filename_hint=text2)
            except requests.RequestException as e:
                print(f"❌ Failed to download {href}: {e}")

    if saved_tables == 0:
        print(f"ℹ No tables found on {url}. If content is JS-rendered, use Selenium.")

# --------------------------------
# Main
# --------------------------------
def find_wioa_etpl() -> None:
    ensure_output()
    soup = get_html(START_URL)
    candidates = find_candidate_links(soup, START_URL)
    if not candidates:
        print("⚠ No candidate links mentioning WIOA/ETPL found on the training page.")
        return

    print("🔎 Candidate links (top 10):")
    for i, (score, url, text) in enumerate(candidates[:10], start=1):
        print(f"  {i}. score={score} | text='{text}' | url={url}")

    best_score, best_url, best_text = candidates[0]
    print(f"\n➡ Processing best match: score={best_score}, text='{best_text}', url={best_url}\n")
    process_candidate(best_url, best_text)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```{python}
import os
import re
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Optional

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd
from tqdm import tqdm
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

BASE_URL = "https://montanaworks.gov"
START_URL = "https://montanaworks.gov/training"
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("montanaworks_wioa_etpl")
SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.headers.update({
    "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) "
                  "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
                  "Chrome/123.0 Safari/537.36 Nan-WIOA-ETPL-Fetcher"
})

REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 20
DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0

DOWNLOAD_EXTS = {".csv", ".xlsx", ".xls", ".json", ".pdf"}

# Terms we consider as signals for the ETPL/WIOA list
TEXT_TERMS = [
    "wioa",
    "eligible training provider",
    "eligible training provider list",
    "etpl"
]
URL_TERMS = [
    "wioa", "etpl", "eligible-training", "eligible_training"
]


def ensure_output():
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def clean_filename(name: str) -> str:
    name = re.sub(r"[^\w\-.]+", "_", name).strip("_")
    return name[:150] or "file"



def get_html(url: str) -> BeautifulSoup:
    """
    Basic HTML fetch using requests, with a polite delay and error handling.
    """
    time.sleep(DELAY_SECONDS)
    resp = SESSION.get(url, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "lxml")



def score_link(a_tag, page_url: str) -> Tuple[int, str]:
    """
    Score a candidate link for relevance to WIOA ETPL.
    Higher score means more likely to be the list we want.
    Returns (score, absolute_url)
    """
    href = a_tag.get("href")
    text = a_tag.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    if not href:
        return (0, "")
    abs_url = urljoin(page_url, href)

    score = 0
    txt = (text or "").lower()
    url_lower = abs_url.lower()

    # Text signals
    for term in TEXT_TERMS:
        if term in txt:
            score += 5

    # URL signals
    for term in URL_TERMS:
        if term in url_lower:
            score += 3

    # Prefer direct data files
    ext = Path(urlparse(abs_url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        score += 2

    # Prefer staying within /training
    if urlparse(abs_url).path.startswith("/training"):
        score += 1

    return (score, abs_url)


def find_candidate_links(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str, str]]:
    """
    Return a list of (score, url, link_text), sorted by score(desc).
    """
    candidates = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        score, abs_url = score_link(a, page_url)
        if score > 0:
            candidates.append((score, abs_url, a.get_text(" ", strip=True)))
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
    return candidates


def download_file(url: str, filename_hint: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Path]:
    """
    Download file to OUTPUT_DIR and return the saved path.
    """
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    ext = Path(parsed.path).suffix.lower()
    fname = filename_hint or Path(parsed.path).name or "download"
    if ext and not fname.lower().endswith(ext):
        fname += ext
    fname = clean_filename(fname)
    out_path = OUTPUT_DIR / fname

    with SESSION.get(url, stream=True, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        total = int(r.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        chunk = 1024 * 64
        with open(out_path, "wb") as f, tqdm(
            total=total if total > 0 else None,
            unit="B", unit_scale=True, unit_divisor=1024,
            desc=f"Downloading {fname}",
            leave=False
        ) as pbar:
            for c in r.iter_content(chunk_size=chunk):
                if c:
                    f.write(c)
                    if total > 0:
                        pbar.update(len(c))
    print(f"✔ Saved file: {out_path}")
    return out_path


def save_tables_from_page(soup: BeautifulSoup, page_url: str) -> int:
    """
    Extract HTML tables on the page and save as CSV into OUTPUT_DIR.
    """
    html = str(soup)
    try:
        tables = pd.read_html(html)
    except ValueError:
        tables = []

    if not tables:
        return 0

    slug = clean_filename(Path(urlparse(page_url).path).name or "training")
    count = 0
    for i, df in enumerate(tables, start=1):
        out_path = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{slug}_table_{i}.csv"
        df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
        count += 1
    print(f"✔ Extracted {count} table(s) from {page_url}")
    return count


def process_candidate(url: str, link_text: str) -> None:
    """
    If candidate is a direct file -> download
    Else -> open page and try to find tables or more specific download links
    """
    ext = Path(urlparse(url).path).suffix.lower()
    if ext in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
        download_file(url, filename_hint=link_text or Path(urlparse(url).path).name)
        return

    # Not a direct file: open the page
    try:
        soup = get_html(url)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"❌ Failed to open {url}: {e}")
        return

    # Try tables first
    saved_tables = save_tables_from_page(soup, url)

    # Also search on this page for more direct file links
    file_links = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = urljoin(url, a["href"])
        ext2 = Path(urlparse(href).path).suffix.lower()
        if ext2 in DOWNLOAD_EXTS:
            text2 = a.get_text(" ", strip=True) or Path(urlparse(href).path).name
            # Give preference if the text contains our ETPL terms
            score = 0
            t2 = text2.lower()
            for term in TEXT_TERMS:
                if term in t2:
                    score += 3
            file_links.append((score, href, text2))

    file_links.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)

    for _, href, text2 in file_links:
        try:
            download_file(href, filename_hint=text2)
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            print(f"❌ Failed to download {href}: {e}")

    if saved_tables == 0 and not file_links:
        print(f"ℹ No tables or data files found on {url}. "
              f"Try the Selenium option if content is JS-rendered.")


def find_wioa_etpl():
    ensure_output()

    # Load the training start page
    try:
        soup = get_html(START_URL)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"❌ Failed to open {START_URL}: {e}")
        return

    # Find candidate links on the training page
    candidates = find_candidate_links(soup, START_URL)

    if not candidates:
        print("⚠ No candidate links mentioning WIOA/ETPL found on the training page.")
    else:
        print("🔎 Candidate links (top 10 shown):")
        for i, (score, url, text) in enumerate(candidates[:10], start=1):
            print(f"  {i}. score={score} | text='{text}' | url={url}")

    # Pick the best candidate and process it
    if candidates:
        best_score, best_url, best_text = candidates[0]
        print(f"\n➡ Processing best match: score={best_score}, text='{best_text}', url={best_url}\n")
        process_candidate(best_url, best_text)

    # Save a small manifest
    manifest = {
        "start_url": START_URL,
    }
    with open(OUTPUT_DIR / "manifest.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
    print(f"📒 Wrote manifest to {OUTPUT_DIR / 'manifest.json'}")
    print("✅ Done.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    find_wioa_etpl()



```

```{python}

# Only needed if requests/BeautifulSoup didn't find what you expect.
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import time

def get_html_via_selenium(url: str) -> Tuple[str, BeautifulSoup]:
    options = webdriver.ChromeOptions()
    options.add_argument("--headless=new")
    driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=Service(ChromeDriverManager().install()), options=options)
    try:
        driver.get(url)
        time.sleep(2.5)  # allow JS to render; tune if needed
        html = driver.page_source
        soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "lxml")
        return html, soup
    finally:
        driver.quit()
```

# Training Enrollment Rate Over Time
```{r}

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)

# ---- 1) Enter the data ----
df <- tribble(
  ~PY,    ~Single_Total, ~Single_Training, ~Repeat_Total, ~Repeat_Training,
# "PY 2017",     1815,           953,              81,               37,
  "PY 2018",     3687,          1983,             150,               95,
  "PY 2019",     3492,          1865,             148,               72,
  "PY 2020",     3585,          1909,             149,               78,
  "PY 2021",     6017,          1906,             251,               71,
  "PY 2022",     5823,          1421,             249,               69,
  "PY 2023",     4367,          1112,             214,               36,
  "PY 2024",     2898,          1147,             147,               68
) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(stringr::str_remove(PY, "PY")))

# ---- 2) Compute enrollment rates ----
df_rates <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Single_Total, Single_Training, Repeat_Total, Repeat_Training),
    names_to = c("Cohort", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(Single|Repeat)_(Total|Training)"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Cohort = dplyr::recode(Cohort,
                    "Single" = "Single",
                    "Repeat" = "Repeat"),
    EnrollRate = Training / Total
  )


# ---- 3) Plot A: Time series of enrollment rates with a smooth fit ----
p_rate <- ggplot(df_rates, aes(x = Year, y = EnrollRate, color = Cohort)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, 
              #span = 0.8, 
              linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = df_rates$Year) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Single" = "#8ad4df",
      "Repeat" = "#09527d"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Training Enrollment Rate Over Time",
    subtitle = "Single vs. Repeat (PY 2018 – PY 2024)",
    x = "Program Year",
    y = " Training Enrollment Rate",
    color = "Cohort"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
   theme( plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),    # Centers the title
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5) )


print(p_rate)

# ---- 4) Plot B: Relationship between Total Participants and Training Enrolled ----
# Scatter with linear fit per cohort
p_scatter <- ggplot(df_rates, aes(x = Total, y = Total, color = Cohort)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Training Enrolled vs. Total Participants",
    subtitle = "Linear fit by cohort",
    x = "Total Participants",
    y = "Training Enrolled",
    color = "Cohort"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_scatter)

# ---- 5) (Optional) Quick linear trend checks for reporting ----
# Rate ~ Year per cohort
trend_summary <- df_rates %>%
  group_by(Cohort) %>%
  do({
    m <- lm(EnrollRate ~ Year, data = .)
    broom::tidy(m)
  })

print(trend_summary)

# ---- 6) (Optional) Save figures ----
# ggsave("enrollment_rate_timeseries.png", p_rate, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
# ggsave("enrolled_vs_total_scatter.png", p_scatter, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(color = "#1280bf", size = 1) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = df_gap$Year) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Gap Over Time (Single – Repeat)",
    subtitle = "Positive values: Single older; Negative values: Repeat older",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Age Gap (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(forcats)
library(broom)

# ---- 1) Enter the data (Single = once enroll; Repeat = repeat participant) ----
barrier_counts <- tribble(
  ~Cohort, ~Barrier,        ~Status,    ~Count,
  "Single","Disabled",      "yes",      868,
  "Single","Disabled",      "no",       8985,
  "Single","Disabled",      "unknown",  662,
  "Single","Low income",    "yes",      7325,
  "Single","Low income",    "no",       3106,
  "Single","Low income",    "unknown",  84,
  "Single","Ex offender",   "yes",      788,
  "Single","Ex offender",   "no",       9571,
  "Single","Ex offender",   "unknown",  156,
  "Single","Single Parent", "yes",      1651,
  "Single","Single Parent", "no",       7662,
  "Single","Single Parent", "unknown",  1202,
  "Repeat","Disabled",      "yes",      34,
  "Repeat","Disabled",      "no",       384,
  "Repeat","Disabled",      "unknown",  23,
  "Repeat","Low income",    "yes",      376,
  "Repeat","Low income",    "no",       64,
  "Repeat","Low income",    "unknown",  1,
  "Repeat","Ex offender",   "yes",      41,
  "Repeat","Ex offender",   "no",       396,
  "Repeat","Ex offender",   "unknown",  4,
  "Repeat","Single Parent", "yes",      107,
  "Repeat","Single Parent", "no",       291,
  "Repeat","Single Parent", "unknown",  43
)

# Fix label casing & factor order for readability
barrier_counts <- barrier_counts %>%
  mutate(
    Barrier = fct_relevel(Barrier, "Low income", "Single Parent", "Disabled", "Ex offender"),
    Status  = fct_relevel(Status, "yes", "no", "unknown")
  )

# ---- 2) Compute totals & shares ----
barrier_shares <- barrier_counts %>%
  group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
  mutate(BarrierTotal = sum(Count)) %>%          # total per cohort-barrier
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(Cohort) %>%
  mutate(CohortTotal = sum(Count[Status != "unknown"])) %>% # optional: cohort total excluding unknowns
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Share = Count / BarrierTotal)

# YES rates per barrier & cohort
yes_rates <- barrier_counts %>%
  filter(Status == "yes") %>%
  group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
  summarize(Yes = sum(Count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    barrier_counts %>%
      filter(Status %in% c("yes", "no")) %>%     # exclude 'unknown' from rate denominator (common practice)
      group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
      summarize(Den = sum(Count), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Cohort", "Barrier")
  ) %>%
  mutate(YesRate = Yes / Den)

# Unknown rates per barrier & cohort
unknown_rates <- barrier_counts %>%
  filter(Status == "unknown") %>%
  group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
  summarize(Unknown = sum(Count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    barrier_counts %>%
      group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
      summarize(Total = sum(Count), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Cohort", "Barrier")
  ) %>%
  mutate(UnknownRate = Unknown / Total)

# ---- 3) Plot A: YES rates by barrier (side-by-side) ----
p_yes <- ggplot(yes_rates, aes(x = Barrier, y = YesRate, fill = Cohort)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(YesRate, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, max(yes_rates$YesRate) * 1.15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Single" = "#1280bf", "Repeat" = "#09527d")) +
  labs(
    title = "Prevalence of Barriers (YES rate by cohort)",
    subtitle = "Denominator excludes 'unknown' responses",
    x = "Barrier", y = "Yes rate", fill = "Cohort"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_yes)

# ---- 4) Plot B: 100% stacked bars (Yes/No/Unknown) faceted by barrier ----
p_stack <- ggplot(barrier_shares, aes(x = Cohort, y = Share, fill = Status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Barrier, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("yes" = "#1280bf", "no" = "#95c6e8", "unknown" = "#d9e9f5")) +
  labs(
    title = "Response Composition by Barrier and Cohort",
    subtitle = "100% stacked bars show proportions of Yes / No / Unknown",
    x = NULL, y = "Share", fill = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p_stack)

# ---- 5) Plot C: Unknown rate by barrier (side-by-side) ----
p_unknown <- ggplot(unknown_rates, aes(x = Barrier, y = UnknownRate, fill = Cohort)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(UnknownRate, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, max(unknown_rates$UnknownRate) * 1.15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Single" = "#1280bf", "Repeat" = "#09527d")) +
  labs(
    title = "Unknown Response Rate by Barrier",
    subtitle = "Higher 'unknown' can mask true prevalence and affect comparisons",
    x = "Barrier", y = "Unknown rate", fill = "Cohort"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

print(p_unknown)

# ---- 6) (Optional) Quick proportion tests: Repeat vs Single for 'Yes' ----
prop_tests <- barrier_counts %>%
  filter(Status %in% c("yes", "no")) %>%
  group_by(Barrier, Cohort, Status) %>%
  summarize(Count = sum(Count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Cohort, Status), values_from = Count) %>%
  mutate(
    # For each barrier, test difference in proportions: Repeat_yes/Repeat_den vs Single_yes/Single_den
    Repeat_den = Repeat_yes + Repeat_no,
    Single_den = Single_yes + Single_no
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    ptest = list(broom::tidy(prop.test(
      x = c(Repeat_yes, Single_yes),
      n = c(Repeat_den, Single_den)
    ))),
    rr = (Repeat_yes / Repeat_den) / (Single_yes / Single_den)
  ) %>%
  unnest(ptest) %>%
  select(Barrier, rr, estimate1, estimate2, p.value, conf.low, conf.high)

print(prop_tests)
# 'rr' is the risk ratio (Repeat vs Single); estimates are Repeat and Single Yes rates.
# Use p.value to assess significance; conf.low/high are CI for difference in proportions.
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# ---- 1) Data (as in your earlier script) ----
barrier_counts <- tribble(
  ~Cohort, ~Barrier,        ~Status,    ~Count,
  "Single","Disabled",      "yes",      868,

  "Repeat","Ex offender",   "yes",      41,
  "Repeat","Ex offender",   "no",       396,

  "Repeat","Single Parent", "yes",      107,

  "Repeat","Single Parent", "unknown",  43
) %>%
  mutate(

    Status  = fct_relevel(Status, "yes", "no", "unknown")
  )

# ---- 2) YES rates (exclude unknown from denominator) ----
yes_rates <- barrier_counts %>%
  filter(Status == "yes") %>%
  group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
  summarize(Yes = sum(Count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    barrier_counts %>%
      filter(Status %in% c("yes", "no")) %>%
      group_by(Cohort, Barrier) %>%
      summarize(Den = sum(Count), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Cohort", "Barrier")
  ) %>%
  mutate(YesRate = Yes / Den)

# ---- 3) Proportion tests (Repeat vs Single) + stars + y positions ----
prop_counts <- barrier_counts %>%
  filter(Status %in% c("yes", "no")) %>%
  group_by(Barrier, Cohort, Status) %>%
  summarize(n = sum(Count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Cohort, Status), values_from = n)

prop_tests <- prop_counts %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Repeat_den = Repeat_yes + Repeat_no,
    Single_den = Single_yes + Single_no,
    test = list(prop.test(x = c(Repeat_yes, Single_yes),
                          n = c(Repeat_den, Single_den))),
    p_value = test$p.value,
    stars = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    repeat_rate = Repeat_yes / Repeat_den,
    single_rate = Single_yes / Single_den,
    # place star above the taller bar for each barrier
    y_text = max(repeat_rate, single_rate) + 0.05
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Barrier, p_value, stars, y_text)

# ---- 4) Plot A (from your earlier code) ----
p_yes <- ggplot(yes_rates, aes(x = Barrier, y = YesRate, fill = Cohort)) +

# ---- 5) Add significance stars + adjust ylim so they are visible ----

    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  # ensure stars aren't clipped
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max(prop_tests$y_text) + 0.02))

print(p_yes_annot)

print(p_yes_bracket)
```

## Correlation Analysis

Once 
```{r}

# Install once if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "janitor", "ggcorrplot"))

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggcorrplot)

# 1) Select variables for correlation (excluding CIP for this plot)
once_cor <- once_final %>%
  select(Gender, Education, Hispanic, African, Ex_Offender, Low_income,
         English_Learner, Single_Parent, Cross_Cultural, Disability,Wages)

# 2) Make Education ordered (edit the levels to match your actual data!)
if ("Education" %in% names(once_cor) && !is.numeric(once_cor$Education)) {
  edu_levels <- c("Less than HS", "High School", "Some College", "Associate",
                  "Bachelor", "Graduate")  # <-- adjust to match your data
  # Only apply if these levels are present; otherwise skip
  if (all(unique(na.omit(once_cor$Education)) %in% edu_levels)) {
    once_cor$Education <- factor(once_cor$Education,
                                 levels = edu_levels,
                                 ordered = TRUE)
    # Convert ordered factor to integer scale 1..K
    once_cor$Education <- as.integer(once_cor$Education)
  } else {
    message("Education mapping skipped: levels in your data differ from edu_levels.")
  }
}

# 3) Convert logicals and two-level factors to numeric 0/1
to01_if_binary_factor <- function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) == 2) {
    return(as.integer(x) - 1L) # maps first level to 0, second to 1
  } else if (is.logical(x)) {
    return(as.integer(x)) # TRUE=1, FALSE=0
  } else {
    return(x)
  }
}

once_num <- once_cor %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), to01_if_binary_factor)) %>%
  # If any character columns slipped in, try to coerce to numeric quietly
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) %>%
  # Keep only numeric columns for correlation
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  clean_names()  # snake_case names (e.g., wages)

# 4) Build correlation matrix using Spearman (robust for ordinal/binary)
cor_mat <- cor(once_num, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# 5) Compute p-values for significance stars/blanks
cor_pmat <- function(mat, method = "spearman") {
  n <- ncol(mat)
  p.mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n,
                  dimnames = list(colnames(mat), colnames(mat)))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], method = method))
      p.mat[i, j] <- test$p.value
    }
  }
  p.mat
}
p.mat <- cor_pmat(once_num)

# 6) Plot the correlation heatmap
ggcorrplot(
  cor_mat,
  hc.order = TRUE,          # hierarchical clustering for layout
  type = "lower",
  lab = TRUE,               # show correlation numbers
  p.mat = p.mat,
  sig.level = 0.05,         # blank non-significant cells
  insig = "blank",
  lab_size = 3,
  colors = c("#2B8CBE", "white", "#D94801"),
  title = "Correlation Heatmap – Workforce Indicators & Wages",
  tl.cex = 10
)

# 7) Optional: focus on correlations with Wages (sorted bar chart)
cor_wages <- sort(cor_mat[, "wages"], decreasing = TRUE)
wages_df <- tibble(var = names(cor_wages),
                   corr_with_wages = as.numeric(cor_wages)) %>%
  filter(var != "wages")

ggplot(wages_df,
       aes(x = reorder(var, corr_with_wages), y = corr_with_wages,
           fill = corr_with_wages > 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2B8CBE", "#D94801"),
                    labels = c("Negative", "Positive"),
                    name = "Direction") +
  labs(title = "Single Participant Correlation with Wages (Spearman)",
       x = NULL, y = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")


```

# Pearson
```{r}
# Install once if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggcorrplot"))

library(tidyverse)
library(ggcorrplot)

# 1) Start from your selection
df <- once_final %>%
  select(Gender, Education, Hispanic, African, Ex_Offender, Low_income,
         English_Learner, Single_Parent, Cross_Cultural, CIP, Wages)

# ---- Option: choose whether to include CIP via dummies ----
include_cip <- FALSE   # set TRUE to include top CIP categories as dummies

# 2) Convert Education to ordered numeric (adjust levels to match your data)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Education = case_when(
      is.numeric(Education) ~ Education,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(factor(
        Education,
        levels = c("Less than HS", "High School", "Some College",
                   "Associate", "Bachelor", "Graduate"),
        ordered = TRUE
      ))
    )
  )

# 3) Convert binary factors/logicals/2-level characters to 0/1
to01 <- function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) == 2) {
    as.integer(x) - 1L
  } else if (is.character(x)) {
    ux <- unique(na.omit(x))
    if (length(ux) == 2) as.integer(factor(x, levels = ux)) - 1L else x
  } else if (is.logical(x)) {
    as.integer(x)
  } else x
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(Gender, Hispanic, African, Ex_Offender, Low_income,
      English_Learner, Single_Parent, Cross_Cultural),
    to01
  ))

# 4) CIP handling
if (!include_cip) {
  df_num <- df %>% select(-CIP)
} else {
  # Keep the top K most frequent CIP categories; collapse the rest to "Other"
  top_k <- 10
  top_cips <- df %>%
    count(CIP, sort = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_k) %>%
    pull(CIP)

  df_num <- df %>%
    mutate(CIP = if_else(CIP %in% top_cips, CIP, "Other")) %>%
    mutate(CIP = factor(CIP)) %>%
    bind_cols(as_tibble(model.matrix(~ CIP - 1, .))) %>%
    select(-CIP)
}

# 5) Keep numeric columns only
df_num <- df_num %>% select(where(is.numeric))

# 6) Pearson correlation matrix
cor_mat <- cor(df_num, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# 7) p-values for each pair (for significance masking)
cor_pmat <- function(dat, method = "pearson") {
  n <- ncol(dat)
  p <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n, dimnames = list(colnames(dat), colnames(dat)))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(dat[, i], dat[, j], method = method))
      p[i, j] <- test$p.value
    }
  }
  p
}
p.mat <- cor_pmat(df_num)

# 8) Plot heatmap (non-significant cells are blank)
ggcorrplot(
  cor_mat,
  type = "lower",
  hc.order = TRUE,     # cluster similar variables
  lab = TRUE,          # numeric labels
  p.mat = p.mat,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  insig = "blank",
  lab_size = 3,
  colors = c("#2B8CBE", "white", "#D94801"),
  title = "Pearson Correlation – Workforce Characteristics & Wages"
)

# 9) Optional: sorted bar chart of correlations with Wages
if ("Wages" %in% colnames(cor_mat)) {
  cor_wages <- sort(cor_mat[, "Wages"], decreasing = TRUE)
  wages_df <- tibble(var = names(cor_wages), corr_with_wages = as.numeric(cor_wages)) %>%
    filter(var != "Wages")

  ggplot(wages_df,
         aes(x = reorder(var, corr_with_wages), y = corr_with_wages,
             fill = corr_with_wages > 0)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2B8CBE", "#D94801"),
                      labels = c("Negative", "Positive"),
                      name = "Direction") +
    labs(title = "Pearson Correlation with Wages",
         x = NULL, y = "Correlation") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}


```


## Ananlysis the relationship between CIP and barrier
```{r}
# Install once if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "DescTools", "broom", "vcd", "nnet", "ggplot2", "ggpubr"))

library(tidyverse)
library(DescTools)
library(broom)
library(vcd)
library(nnet)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# --- Options: Unknown=9 handling & CIP collapsing ---
treat_9_as_na <- TRUE     # set FALSE to keep "Unknown" as a category
min_cip_n     <- 300     # collapse CIP levels with < min_cip_n cases into "Other"
use_top_k     <- NA       # alternatively, set to an integer (e.g., 10) to keep top K CIP

# --- 1) Select variables (adapt once_final) ---
dat_single <- once_final %>%
  select(CIP, Low_income, English_Learner, Cross_Cultural, Ex_Offender,
         Age, Education, Single_Parent, Disability)

dat_single$CIP<- substr(dat_single$CIP, 1,2)

dat_single <- dat_single %>% filter(CIP != "99")

dat_repeat <- repeat_final %>%
  select(CIP, Low_income, English_Learner, Cross_Cultural, Ex_Offender,
         Age, Education, Single_Parent, Disability)

dat_repeat$CIP<- substr(dat_repeat$CIP, 1,2)

dat_repeat <- dat_repeat %>% filter(CIP != "99")

# --- 2) Helpers ---
recode_9 <- function(x) ifelse(x == 9, NA, x)

to_binary_factor <- function(x, labels = c("No", "Yes")) {
  ux <- sort(unique(na.omit(x)))
  if (length(ux) == 2 && all(ux %in% c(0, 1))) {
    factor(x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = labels)
  } else {
    factor(x)
  }
}
###########################################
# --- 3) Clean variables ---
dat_single<- dat_single %>%
  mutate(CIP = factor(CIP),
         Age = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Age)),
         Education = factor(Education, ordered = TRUE))  # label later if desired

if (treat_9_as_na) {
  dat_single <- dat_single %>%
    mutate(Cross_Cultural = recode_9(Cross_Cultural),
           Single_Parent  = recode_9(Single_Parent),
           Disability = recode_9(Disability))
}

dat_single <- dat_single %>%
  mutate(
    Low_income      = to_binary_factor(Low_income),
    English_Learner = to_binary_factor(English_Learner),
    Cross_Cultural  = to_binary_factor(Cross_Cultural),
    Ex_Offender     = to_binary_factor(Ex_Offender),
    Single_Parent   = to_binary_factor(Single_Parent),
    Disability      = to_binary_factor(Disability)
  )

# --- 4) Collapse rare CIP levels to reduce sparsity ---
cip_counts_single <- dat_single %>% count(CIP, sort = TRUE)

if (!is.na(use_top_k)) {
  keep_levels <- cip_counts %>% slice_head(n = use_top_k) %>% pull(CIP)
} else {
  keep_levels <- cip_counts_single %>% filter(n >= min_cip_n) %>% pull(CIP)
}
dat_single <- dat_single %>%
  mutate(CIP = if_else( CIP %in% keep_levels, as.character(CIP), "Other")) %>%
  mutate(CIP2 = factor(CIP))

# --- 5) CIP profiles: prevalence & lift ---
binary_vars <- c("Low_income", "English_Learner", "Cross_Cultural",
                 "Ex_Offender", "Single_Parent","Disability")

overall_prev <- dat_single %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(binary_vars), ~ mean(.x == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "overall_rate")

cip_profiles_single <- dat_single %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(binary_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(value = fct_explicit_na(value, na_level = "Missing")) %>%
  group_by(CIP, variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    yes_rate = mean(value == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_rate = mean(value == "Missing", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(overall_prev, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(lift = yes_rate / overall_rate)

# Plot lift by CIP (higher = concentration)
CIP_single <-ggplot(cip_profiles_single, aes(x = reorder(variable, lift), y = lift, fill = CIP)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Lift of Binary Characteristics by CIP Cluster",
       x = NULL, y = "Lift (Cluster Yes Rate / Overall Yes Rate)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
####################################
# --- 3) Clean variables ---
dat_repeat<- dat_repeat %>%
  mutate(CIP = factor(CIP),
         Age = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Age)),
         Education = factor(Education, ordered = TRUE))  # label later if desired

if (treat_9_as_na) {
  dat_repeat <- dat_repeat %>%
    mutate(Cross_Cultural = recode_9(Cross_Cultural),
           Single_Parent  = recode_9(Single_Parent),
           Disability = recode_9(Disability))
}

dat_repeat <- dat_repeat %>%
  mutate(
    Low_income      = to_binary_factor(Low_income),
    English_Learner = to_binary_factor(English_Learner),
    Cross_Cultural  = to_binary_factor(Cross_Cultural),
    Ex_Offender     = to_binary_factor(Ex_Offender),
    Single_Parent   = to_binary_factor(Single_Parent),
    Disability      = to_binary_factor(Disability)
  )

# --- 4) Collapse rare CIP levels to reduce sparsity ---
cip_counts_repeat <- dat_repeat %>% count(CIP, sort = TRUE)

if (!is.na(use_top_k)) {
  keep_levels <- cip_counts %>% slice_head(n = use_top_k) %>% pull(CIP)
} else {
  keep_levels <- cip_counts_repeat %>% filter(n >= 20) %>% pull(CIP)
}
dat_repeat <- dat_repeat %>%
  mutate(CIP = if_else( CIP %in% keep_levels, as.character(CIP), "Other")) %>%
  mutate(CIP2 = factor(CIP))

# --- 5) CIP profiles: prevalence & lift ---
binary_vars <- c("Low_income", "English_Learner", "Cross_Cultural",
                 "Ex_Offender", "Single_Parent","Disability")

overall_prev_repeat <- dat_repeat %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(binary_vars), ~ mean(.x == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "overall_rate")

cip_profiles_repeat <- dat_repeat %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(binary_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(value = fct_explicit_na(value, na_level = "Missing")) %>%
  group_by(CIP, variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    yes_rate = mean(value == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_rate = mean(value == "Missing", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(overall_prev_repeat, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(lift = yes_rate / overall_rate)

# Plot lift by CIP (higher = concentration)
CIP_repeat <-ggplot(cip_profiles_repeat, aes(x = reorder(variable, lift), y = lift, fill = CIP)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Lift of Binary Characteristics by CIP Cluster",
       x = NULL, y = "Lift (Cluster Yes Rate / Overall Yes Rate)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
CIP_repeat <- ggplot(cip_profiles_repeat, aes(x = reorder(variable,lift), y = lift, fill = CIP)) +

# Combine side-by-side with shared legend and a single overall title

  plot_annotation(title = "Training programs vs. Barriers Analysis",

                             1.0 = same as overall population.\n
                             >1.0 = over-represented.\n

    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "italic", color = "darkgray")
  )

# If you want the legend to wrap into two rows (useful if labels are long), add:

# Print
combined_plot
```

```{r}
                                  levels = cip_levels, labels = cip_labels)

# 2) Build a single, shared order for 'variable' across BOTH datasets

#    - Order by average lift across both (you can change to alphabetical if preferred)

  cip_profiles_repeat %>% select(variable, lift)
) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarize(mean_lift = mean(lift, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%

  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = var_levels))

  scale_fill_manual(values = my_color, name = "CIP") +
```

## Program Successful Analysis

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(lme4)        # mixed-effects GLMM
library(splines)     # restricted cubic splines
library(ggeffects)   # marginal effects / predicted probabilities
library(pROC)        # ROC/AUC
library(patchwork)   # combine plots
library(car)         # VIF

# Inspect
str(once_succ)
```


```{r}
# Recode basics (adjust labels as needed)
df <- once_succ %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = factor(Gender, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    Employment_Entry = factor(Employment_Entry, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Low_income = factor(Low_income, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Credential = factor(Credential, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    Employed = factor(round(Employed), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")), # ensure binary
    Education = ordered(Education),   # treat as ordinal (if codes reflect levels)
    County = factor(County)           # many counties; useful for random intercept
  )


#####Descriptive & Bivariate Checks

# Bivariate tests (illustrative)
# Categorical vs outcome: Chi-squared
chisq.test(table(df$Credential, df$Low_income))
chisq.test(table(df$Employed,   df$Employment_Entry))

# Continuous vs outcome: t-test or Wilcoxon
t.test(Length ~ Credential, data = df)
t.test(Length ~ Employed,   data = df)


```

# Logistic Models
```{r}

# Model A: Credential (GLM with logit, splines for Age/Length)
m_cred <- glm(
  Credential ~ Gender + Employment_Entry + ns(Age, df = 4) +
    Education  + Low_income + ns(Length, df = 4),
  data = df, family = binomial()
)

# Model B: Employed (exclude Credential per your spec)
m_empl <- glm(
  Employed ~ Gender + Employment_Entry + ns(Age, df = 4) +
    Education +  Low_income + ns(Length, df = 4),
  data = df, family = binomial()
)

# (Optional) Model C: Employed with Credential included
m_empl_cred <- glm(
  Employed ~ Credential + Gender + Employment_Entry + ns(Age, df = 4) +
    Education + Low_income + ns(Length, df = 4),
  data = df, family = binomial()
)

summary(m_cred)
summary(m_empl)
summary(m_empl_cred)

# Check multicollinearity (GLMs; VIF ignores splines so interpret cautiously)
car::vif(m_cred)
car::vif(m_empl)


```

## County Random Intercept


```{r}

# Mixed-effects GLMMs
glmm_cred <- glmer(
  Credential ~ Gender + Employment_Entry + ns(Age, 4) + Education +
    Low_income + ns(Length, 4) + (1 | County),
  data = df, family = binomial(), control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

glmm_empl <- glmer(
  Employed ~ Gender + Employment_Entry + ns(Age, 4) + Education +
    Low_income + ns(Length, 4) + (1 | County),
  data = df, family = binomial(), control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
```

```{r}
# AUC for GLMs
pred_cred <- predict(m_cred, type = "response")
pred_empl <- predict(m_empl, type = "response")

roc_cred <- pROC::roc(m_cred$y, pred_cred)
roc_empl <- pROC::roc(m_empl$y, pred_empl)

pROC::auc(roc_cred)
pROC::auc(roc_empl)


# Simple calibration plot function
cal_plot <- function(outcome, pred, title){
  tibble(outcome = as.numeric(outcome) - 1, pred = pred) %>%
    mutate(bin = ntile(pred, 10)) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarize(mean_pred = mean(pred), mean_obs = mean(outcome), n = n()) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = mean_pred, y = mean_obs)) +
    geom_point() + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey40") +
    labs(x = "Predicted probability", y = "Observed rate", title = title) +
    theme_minimal()
}

p_cal_cred <- cal_plot(m_cred$y, pred_cred, "Calibration: Credential")
p_cal_empl <- cal_plot(m_empl$y,   pred_empl, "Calibration: Employed")
p_cal_cred + p_cal_empl
```

```{r}
# Tidy, exponentiate (OR), and plot for Model A and Model B
plot_or <- function(model, title){
  coefs <- broom::tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(term = str_replace(term, "ns\\(Age, df = 4\\).*", "Age (spline)"),
           term = str_replace(term, "ns\\(Length, df = 4\\).*", "Length (spline)"))
  
  ggplot(coefs, aes(x = reorder(term, estimate), y = estimate)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.2) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Odds Ratio (logit)", title = title) +
    theme_minimal()
}

p_or_cred <- plot_or(m_cred, "Predictors of Earning a Credential")
p_or_empl <- plot_or(m_empl, "Predictors of Post‑Program Employment")
p_or_cred + p_or_empl
```

```{r}
# SMD helper functions
smd_cont <- function(x, grp) {
  m1 <- mean(x[grp == "Single"], na.rm = TRUE)
  m2 <- mean(x[grp == "Repeat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  s1 <- sd(x[grp == "Single"], na.rm = TRUE)
  s2 <- sd(x[grp == "Repeat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  (m1 - m2) / sqrt((s1^2 + s2^2) / 2)
}

smd_bin <- function(x, grp) {
  p1 <- mean(x[grp == "Single"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  p2 <- mean(x[grp == "Repeat"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  (p1 - p2) / sqrt((p1*(1-p1) + p2*(1-p2)) / 2)
}

smds <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = c("Age", "Length",  "Employment_Entry"),
  SMD = c(
    smd_cont(df$Age, df$cohort),
    smd_cont(df$Length, df$cohort),
    smd_bin(df$Employment_Entry, df$cohort)
  )
)
smds
```

outcome comparison

```{r}
ci_prop <- function(x, grp, label) {
  single_success <- sum(x[grp == "Single"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  single_total   <- sum(!is.na(x[grp == "Single"]))
  repeat_success <- sum(x[grp == "Repeat"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  repeat_total   <- sum(!is.na(x[grp == "Repeat"]))

  single_ci <- prop.test(single_success, single_total, conf.level = 0.90)$conf.int
  repeat_ci <- prop.test(repeat_success, repeat_total, conf.level = 0.90)$conf.int

  out <- data.frame(
    cohort = c("Single", "Repeat"),
    success = c(single_success, repeat_success),
    total   = c(single_total, repeat_total),
    rate    = c(single_success/single_total, repeat_success/repeat_total),
    ci_low  = c(single_ci[1], repeat_ci[1]),
    ci_high = c(single_ci[2], repeat_ci[2]),
    outcome = label
  )

  # Add RR and RD rows (for convenience)
  RR <- out$rate[2] / out$rate[1]
  RD <- out$rate[2] - out$rate[1]
  attr(out, "RR") <- RR
  attr(out, "RD") <- RD
  out
}

employed <- ci_prop(df$Employed, df$cohort, "Employed")
credential <- ci_prop(df$Credential, df$cohort, "Credential")

employed
attr(employed, "RR"); attr(employed, "RD")

credential
attr(credential, "RR"); attr(credential, "RD")
```

# Format the two plot

```{r}

plot_outcome <- function(tbl, col = "#1280bf", ylim = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot(tbl, aes(x = cohort, y = rate)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, color = col) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), width = 0.3, linewidth = 1, color = "#f6851f") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
    labs(
      title = NULL,                   # shared title will be added via patchwork
      y = NULL,                       # we'll control y label per-panel below
      x = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
  
#   if (!is.null(ylim)) {
#     p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim)
#   }
#   p
 }


# Common y-limit so both panels use the same scale
common_ylim <- c(0, max(c(employed$ci_high, credential$ci_high), na.rm = TRUE))

# Build panels (left shows y label, right hides it)
p1 <- plot_outcome(employed,   col = "#1280bf", ylim = common_ylim) + labs(y = "Rate (with 95% CI)", x= "Employment Status After Exited")
p2 <- plot_outcome(credential, col = "#1280bf", ylim = common_ylim) + labs(y = NULL, x= "Credential")

# Combine with shared title
(p1 | p2) +
  plot_annotation(title = "WIOA Performance Outcomes") &
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

## 5) Propensity Score (PS) Weighting
 
```{r}
 # PS model (logistic) for cohort assignment
ps_mod <- glm(cohort ~ Gender + Age + Education + Low_income + Employment_Entry + Length + County,data = df, family = binomial())

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    ps = as.numeric(ps_mod$fitted.values),
    w  = ifelse(cohort == "Repeat", 1/ps, 1/(1-ps))
  )

# Check weight stability
summary(df$w); quantile(df$w, probs = c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE)

# Optional: trim extreme weights (e.g., at 1st and 99th percentiles)
q <- quantile(df$w, probs = c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE)
df_trim <- df %>% filter(w >= q[1], w <= q[2])

# Weighted logistic regressions (cohort only, since weighting accounts for confounding)
mod_emp_w <- glm(Employed ~ cohort, data = df_trim, weights = w, family = binomial())
mod_cred_w <- glm(Credential ~ cohort, data = df_trim, weights = w, family = binomial())

#broom::tidy(mod_emp_w, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
#broom::tidy(mod_cred_w, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)

# Weighted marginal probabilities via emmeans
emm_emp_w <- emmeans(mod_emp_w, ~ cohort, type = "response", weights = "w")
emm_cred_w <- emmeans(mod_cred_w, ~ cohort, type = "response", weights = "w")

emm_emp_w; pairs(emm_emp_w, type = "response")
emm_cred_w; pairs(emm_cred_w, type = "response")
 
```

```{r}
# Plot adjusted marginal probabilities from mixed-effects model
plot_emmeans <- function(emm, title) {
  df_ <- as.data.frame(emm)
  ggplot(df_, aes(x = cohort, y = prob)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), width = 0.08) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
    labs(title = title, y = "Adjusted probability (95% CI)", x = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}

plot_emmeans(emm_emp, "Adjusted Employment Probability by Cohort")
plot_emmeans(emm_cred, "Adjusted Credential Probability by Cohort")
```
